chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from 'Imran al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever buys a sacrificial animal (had'y) and does not know that it has a defect until he pays its price, then learns afterwards, then the transaction is complete (valid)." And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:

key_terms.هَدْياً: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or 'Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I buy a sacrificial animal and later discover it has a defect I didn't know about?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'ghabn farish' (significant undervaluation due to defect) in sacrificial animals, establishing that undisclosed defects do not automatically invalidate the sale if the buyer has already paid. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the burden of due diligence lies with the buyer unless a specific warranty is agreed upon, distinguishing this from cases of fraud. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of *Thibh* (sacrifice) within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, ensuring the validity of the ritual offering despite minor, unknown imperfections.
